result.title: Tiny Recursive Message Passing
result.summary: Message passing neural networks have shown remarkable performance in algorithmic and constraint reasoning, due to their ability to encode the structure of the task directly in the architecture. Recent work has shown that better results can be achieved using recursive transformers trained with deep supervision and truncated recursions, which make extremely deep loops stable to train, and equipped with test-time procedures such as discrete deduction lattices. In this work, we apply the same procedures to message passing networks, and show that the two ingredients are complementary, and lead to parameter efficient models: we obtain about $99\%$ test accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme with a model of $16$k parameters that trains in about $10$ minutes on an H100, or in $9$ hours on a CPU. We further show that the cost of truncating gradients grows with the number of rounds information needs to cross the graph, making the choice of wiring a trade-off between robustness to truncation and transfer across problem sizes. We conclude by showing that our models transfer zero-shot to larger instances than those seen during training, outperforming popular neural baselines on N-queens and Boolean satisfiability with a fraction of their parameters.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作把递归 Transformer 中「深监督＋截断递归」的训练流程搬到消息传递网络上，用于数独、N 皇后与 SAT 等算法推理任务，得到参数极小的模型（约 16k 参数在 Sudoku-Extreme 上近 99% 准确率），并分析梯度截断代价与图上信息传递轮数的关系及零样本迁移到更大规模实例的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文对循环深度、梯度截断与深监督的权衡，以及「鲁棒性 vs 尺寸迁移」的分析，可能为 LVR 中 loop 式 latent 状态更新、训练监督与长度泛化提供可核查的方法线索，需确认其结论能否迁移到多模态内部推理状态。
